encounters.cc: Recurrent oral candidiasis, multiple ear infections since birth, and failure to thrive.

lines: Recurrent oral candidiasis, multiple ear infections since birth, and failure to thrive.
The parents report that the child has had multiple episodes of otitis media and oral candidiasis since birth.
They also note that the infant has not gained weight adequately and appears much smaller than other infants his age.
- Glycogen storage disease type V (McArdle disease)
The child was born at term via normal vaginal delivery with no complications during pregnancy or delivery.
- Vascular ring ligation and division (pending cardiothoracic evaluation)
- Immune globulin (IVIG) 400 mg/kg IV infusion monthly

- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg TMP component orally once daily (prophylaxis)
- Cyclosporine 10 mg/kg/day orally divided BID (for bone marrow suppression)
The family history is notable for a maternal uncle who died in infancy from severe infections, but no formal diagnosis was reported.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).

He is in the 3rd percentile for weight and 5th percentile for height.

- Chest X-ray: Absence of thymic shadow

encounters.cc: Poor weight gain despite adequate caloric intake and recurrent cough with bulky, foul-smelling stools.

lines: Poor weight gain despite adequate caloric intake and recurrent cough with bulky, foul-smelling stools.
The patient presents to Pediatric Gastroenterology two months following his diagnosis of severe combined immunodeficiency in Allergy and Immunology.
The parents report that the child has had multiple episodes of bronchitis since birth and has been hospitalized twice for pneumonia.
They also note that the infant's stools are unusually foul-smelling and bulky.
- Glycogen storage disease type V (McArdle disease)
- Vascular ring ligation and division (pending cardiothoracic evaluation)
- Immune globulin (IVIG) 400 mg/kg IV infusion monthly
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 3000 units lipase per 120 mL of formula or breast milk
- Uncooked cornstarch 1.6 g/kg orally every 4 hours while awake
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg TMP component orally once daily (prophylaxis)
- Cyclosporine 10 mg/kg/day orally divided BID (for bone marrow suppression)
- Maternal uncle: deceased at age 2 from severe infections (suspected X-linked immunodeficiency)
- Older sibling: healthy, no chronic medical conditions
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).
On examination, the child appears malnourished and is below the 5th percentile for weight and height.
His lungs auscultation reveals diffuse wheezes.
The rest of the physical examination is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Progressive pallor, poor feeding, and easy fatigability noted by parents.

lines: Progressive pallor, poor feeding, and easy fatigability noted by parents.

The patient is a 4-month-old male infant with recurrent infections, failure to thrive, and prior evaluations by Allergy and Immunology and Pediatric Gastroenterology who presents to Pediatric Hematology and Oncology.
He is brought by his parents due to concerns about his pale appearance and poor feeding.
They report that he seems to tire easily and has not been gaining weight as expected.
- Glycogen storage disease type V (McArdle disease)
His birth history is notable for a cleft palate, which is scheduled for surgical repair.
- Vascular ring ligation and division (pending cardiothoracic evaluation)
- Immune globulin (IVIG) 400 mg/kg IV infusion monthly
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 3000 units lipase per 120 mL of formula or breast milk
- Uncooked cornstarch 1.6 g/kg orally every 4 hours while awake
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg TMP component orally once daily (prophylaxis)
- Cyclosporine 10 mg/kg/day orally divided BID (for bone marrow suppression)
- Maternal uncle: deceased at age 2 from severe infections (suspected X-linked immunodeficiency)
- Older sibling: healthy, no chronic medical conditions
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).
On physical examination, the infant has a systolic heart murmur and a webbed neck.
His thumbs appear to be abnormally shaped.

encounters.cc: Persistent biphasic stridor and cough since birth with worsening dysphagia upon introduction of solids.

lines: Persistent biphasic stridor and cough since birth with worsening dysphagia upon introduction of solids.

The patient is a 6-month-old male with severe combined immunodeficiency diagnosed in January, cystic fibrosis diagnosed in March, and severe aplastic anemia diagnosed in May, who returns for evaluation of persistent respiratory symptoms.

The infant is brought to the pediatrician by his parents due to a persistent cough and a high-pitched wheezing sound that has been present since birth and seems to worsen when he is feeding or crying.
The parents also report that their child has difficulty swallowing solid foods and has had multiple episodes of vomiting after meals.
The infant's growth has been below the 5th percentile.
- Glycogen storage disease type V (McArdle disease)
- Vascular ring ligation and division (pending cardiothoracic evaluation)
- Immune globulin (IVIG) 400 mg/kg IV infusion monthly
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 3000 units lipase per 120 mL of formula or breast milk
- Uncooked cornstarch 1.6 g/kg orally every 4 hours while awake
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg TMP component orally once daily (prophylaxis)
- Cyclosporine 10 mg/kg/day orally divided BID (for bone marrow suppression)
- Maternal uncle: deceased at age 2 from severe infections (suspected X-linked immunodeficiency)
- Older sibling: healthy, no chronic medical conditions
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).
On physical examination, the infant has biphasic stridor that improves when his neck is extended.
There is no cyanosis or clubbing, and lung auscultation is clear.
A barium swallow study shows an external compression on the posterior wall of the esophagus.
A chest X-ray reveals a right aortic arch.

encounters.cc: Frequent bacterial pneumonia and otitis media recurring shortly after antibiotic courses completed.

lines: Frequent bacterial pneumonia and otitis media recurring shortly after antibiotic courses completed.
The patient returns for ongoing management of his complex history including severe combined immunodeficiency, cystic fibrosis, and recently evaluated severe aplastic anemia and vascular ring.
Since he was around 6 months old, he has had multiple episodes of otitis media and bacterial pneumonia requiring antibiotics.
His parents report that he recovers with treatment but often gets sick again within a few weeks.
He is up to date on routine pediatric visits but has not received live vaccines.
- Glycogen storage disease type V (McArdle disease)
- Vascular ring ligation and division (pending cardiothoracic evaluation)
- Immune globulin (IVIG) 400 mg/kg IV infusion monthly
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 3000 units lipase per 120 mL of formula or breast milk
- Uncooked cornstarch 1.6 g/kg orally every 4 hours while awake
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg TMP component orally once daily (prophylaxis)
- Cyclosporine 10 mg/kg/day orally divided BID (for bone marrow suppression)
- Maternal uncle: deceased at age 2 from severe infections (suspected X-linked immunodeficiency)
- Older sibling: healthy, no chronic medical conditions
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).
On physical examination, he appears well-nourished and interactive.
No tonsillar tissue is visualized, and cervical lymph nodes are not palpable.
Laboratory results reveal markedly reduced levels of all major immunoglobulin classes.
T cell counts are within normal limits.

encounters.cc: Four episodes of acute otitis media in the past five months and recent viral bronchitis.

lines: Four episodes of acute otitis media in the past five months and recent viral bronchitis.
The patient returns to Pediatric Immunology for follow-up of prior evaluations for severe combined immunodeficiency and X-linked agammaglobulinemia.
The parents report that the child has had four ear infections in the past five months.
They are concerned because the child's older sibling did not have this many infections at the same age.
- Glycogen storage disease type V (McArdle disease)
The infant was born at term without complications and has met all developmental milestones.
His immunizations are up to date.
- Vascular ring ligation and division (pending cardiothoracic evaluation)
- Immune globulin (IVIG) 400 mg/kg IV infusion monthly
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 3000 units lipase per 120 mL of formula or breast milk
- Uncooked cornstarch 1.6 g/kg orally every 4 hours while awake
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg TMP component orally once daily (prophylaxis)
- Cyclosporine 10 mg/kg/day orally divided BID (for bone marrow suppression)
- Maternal uncle: deceased at age 2 from severe infections (suspected X-linked immunodeficiency)
- Older sibling: healthy, no chronic medical conditions
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).
On examination, the child is well-appearing, with no signs of dysmorphism or growth retardation.
His weight and height are at the 50th percentile for his age.
Examination of the ears reveals bilateral tympanic membrane retraction without effusion.
The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable.
Laboratory studies are ordered, and the results are as follows:
- Antibody response to vaccines: Protective titers to all administered vaccines

encounters.cc: Acute episode of shakiness, sweating, and irritability upon awakening with progressive abdominal distension.

lines: Acute episode of shakiness, sweating, and irritability upon awakening with progressive abdominal distension.

This 1-year-old male with severe combined immunodeficiency, cystic fibrosis, severe aplastic anemia, and congenital vascular ring followed in multiple subspecialty clinics presents to the emergency department.
The parents report that the baby tires easily during feeding, becomes irritable when meals are delayed, and occasionally appears shaky or sweaty in the early morning.
Over the past two months, the infant has failed to gain weight adequately, and his abdomen has become visibly enlarged.
There is no vomiting or diarrhea.
- Glycogen storage disease type V (McArdle disease)
His vaccinations are up to date,.
- Vascular ring ligation and division (pending cardiothoracic evaluation)
- Immune globulin (IVIG) 400 mg/kg IV infusion monthly
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 3000 units lipase per 120 mL of formula or breast milk
- Uncooked cornstarch 1.6 g/kg orally every 4 hours while awake
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg TMP component orally once daily (prophylaxis)
- Cyclosporine 10 mg/kg/day orally divided BID (for bone marrow suppression)
There is no family history of metabolic disorders or early childhood deaths.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).
On physical examination, the child appears alert but has a protuberant abdomen with hepatomegaly extending 4 cm below the right costal margin.
Muscle tone is mildly decreased in the proximal limbs.
Laboratory studies reveal mild hypoglycemia, elevated aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and a modest rise in creatine kinase.
Lactic acid and uric acid levels are within normal limits.
A liver biopsy shows abnormal glycogen with short outer branches.

encounters.cc: Persistent hepatomegaly and poor exercise tolerance with recurrent fatigue between meals.

lines: Persistent hepatomegaly and poor exercise tolerance with recurrent fatigue between meals.
The patient returns for follow-up evaluation of symptoms initially presenting to the emergency department in July 2021 with acute shakiness, sweating, and abdominal distension.
They report that his abdomen has appeared enlarged for several months and that he seems more fatigued than other infants.
He has difficulty feeding, becomes irritable when meals are delayed, and sometimes trembles or becomes sweaty between feedings.
- McArdle disease (Glycogen Storage Disease Type V) (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- Vascular ring ligation and division (pending cardiothoracic evaluation)
- Immune globulin (IVIG) 400 mg/kg IV infusion monthly
- Pancrelipase (Creon) 3000 units lipase per 120 mL of formula or breast milk
- Uncooked cornstarch 1.6 g/kg orally every 4 hours while awake
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5 mg/kg TMP component orally once daily (prophylaxis)
- Cyclosporine 10 mg/kg/day orally divided BID (for bone marrow suppression)
- Maternal uncle: deceased at age 2 from severe infections (suspected X-linked immunodeficiency)
- Older sibling: healthy, no chronic medical conditions
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).
His growth chart shows weight and length below the 10th percentile.
On physical examination, the child is alert and interactive but has a protuberant abdomen with a firm, enlarged liver palpable 4 cm below the right costal margin.
There is no jaundice or ascites.
Laboratory studies reveal mild hypoglycemia, elevated liver transaminases, and mildly increased creatine kinase.
A liver biopsy demonstrates accumulation of abnormal glycogen with short outer chains.
A fasting challenge shows moderately low blood glucose levels without significant lactic acidosis or hyperuricemia.
Genetic analysis reveals a defect in an enzyme responsible for removing α-1,6 glycosidic linkages from glycogen.
